title: Smoke & regression suite for model snapshots: streaming + tool/function-call conformance
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Create a reusable smoke and regression test suite that verifies streaming semantics and external tool/function-call behavior for every newly onboarded model snapshot (including pinned versions and quantized variants). The suite must exercise resumable streams, partial/structured outputs during tool calls, KV-cache warm/resume scenarios, backpressure handling, and graceful fallback to non-streaming variants. Results are used to gate model catalog publish + performance profile entry.
acceptance_criteria: Automated smoke tests run as part of the model onboarding pipeline and return pass/fail within 30 minutes for typical model sizes.
Regression harness includes at least 25 vectors covering token boundary splits, mid-stream tool invocation, early termination, and structured JSON emission during function calls.
For any failing vector, harness records trace links, a minimal reproducible prompt, and a suggested rollback (pin previous snapshot) + rollback PR template.
Successful runs automatically annotate the model entry in the catalog with a conformance badge and link to the generated performance profile artifact.
Tests validate behavior under both hosted and dedicated routing: streaming fallback, model-variant pinning, and routing policy respects declared compatibility.
Security review checklist is completed for tools/function-call vectors that exercise file/IO or external connectors.
Clear runbook exists for onboarding engineers describing triage steps and how to request manual exemptions for non-conforming but acceptable behaviors.
plan: Define canonical vector set (25+) in a Confluence page and store as JSON fixtures in repo under tests/onboarding/vectors/
Extend existing streaming verifier to include: resumable stream replay, token boundary fuzzing, and partial-JSON validation for function-call payloads
Add a lightweight tool-call simulator that can accept and respond to function-call frames and assert session state correctness
Wire the suite into the model onboarding pipeline: run on each snapshot build, block publish if critical failures observed
Publish a performance-profile artifact (summary CSV + SLO metrics) to the catalog on pass, with conformance badge metadata
Dashboarding: create a per-model onboarding report page with traces, failing vectors, and suggested remediation
Run cross-environment validation for hosted/dev/dedicated, capture any environment-specific fallbacks
Document triage playbook and add to Onboarding runbook.
comments: 2026-02-19 - Aisha Kumar: Initial scoping done. Drafted vector categories and rough estimate. Flagging potential extra work for quantized int4 snapshots.
2026-02-25 - Luca Martin: Implemented token-boundary fuzzing harness prototype. Found inconsistent behavior in two Llama-derived snapshots when streaming resumes after a KV-cache invalidation.
2026-03-01 - Priya Desai (PM): Confirmed gating requirement with catalog team. If critical fails, snapshot publish must be blocked and auto-rollback suggested.
2026-03-04 - Security (review): Requested explicit vectors for any tool-call that triggers outbound HTTP or file-system access. Added to acceptance criteria.
2026-03-09 - Engineering Lead (Jon Park): Review feedback: prefer smaller, faster smoke set for CI and larger regression suite for nightly runs. Adjusted CI timeout to 30 minutes.
2026-03-10 - Luca Martin: Integrated the simulator and added automated artifact publishing. Running cross-environment smoke now; two failing vectors remain (edge-case JSON chunking).
notes: Trade-offs: keeping the smoke suite small reduces CI flakiness but may miss subtle regressions; mitigated by nightly full regression runs.
If a model intentionally diverges (e.g., proprietary tokenization), the onboarding flow should capture an exemption reason and required dev-owner approval.
Consider integrating with Optimize to suggest quantization profiles when failures are tied to precision loss in int4 variants.
We should publish a machine-readable conformance manifest alongside the performance profile so downstream customers can programmatically gate rollouts.
